Stone, rock, wood, dirt: set roughness 0.75–0.95 and metalness 0.0–0.05 explicitly
Metal (ore, armour, coins): roughness 0.10–0.35 and metalness 0.70–1.0
Crystal, glass: roughness 0.0–0.15 and metalness 0.0; add emissive colour for glow
Always set roughness and metalness explicitly on every MeshStandardMaterial — never leave as default (0.5/0.5)

After any vertex position change — including clamping, offsetting, or flat-bottom ops — always call geometry.computeVertexNormals() immediately; never modify positions after computing normals or the normals will be wrong
createAsset() must add geometry to a Mesh and the Mesh to the returned Object3D; never return an empty Group

IcosahedronGeometry and PolyhedronGeometry are non-indexed BufferGeometries: call mergeVertices() immediately after creation to convert to indexed geometry before any displacement. This gives each unique vertex one index, so sequential LCG displacement is consistent (shared_edge_fraction = 1.0, mesh stays connected) and computeVertexNormals() produces smooth shading. Pattern: import { mergeVertices } from "three/examples/jsm/utils/BufferGeometryUtils.js"; ... let geo = new THREE.IcosahedronGeometry(r, d); geo = mergeVertices(geo); // then displace and computeVertexNormals()

Vertex displacement amplitude must stay below 50% of the face edge length to prevent face folding. For IcosahedronGeometry(r, detail): edge_length ≈ r × 1.05 / detail. Safe max displacement = 0.4 × edge_length. At detail=2 (r=0.75): edge≈0.39u → max disp≈0.08u (≈10% of r). At detail=3 (r=0.75): edge≈0.26u → max disp≈0.10u (≈13% of r). Exceeding this causes faces to fold inward; MeshStandardMaterial backface-culls them → visible cracks/splits. Rule: displacement = rand() * MAX where MAX ≤ 0.40 × (r × 1.05 / detail).

IcosahedronGeometry ships with a UV seam: 9 vertex pairs share the same 3D position but have u=0 vs u=1 in their UV attribute. mergeVertices() treats these as distinct because their UV differs, leaving them at separate buffer indices. Sequential LCG displacement then gives each copy a different value, opening a physical gap at the seam → visible crack. Fix: call geo.deleteAttribute('uv') BEFORE mergeVertices(), then set UVs manually after displacement. Pattern: let geo = new THREE.IcosahedronGeometry(r, d); geo.deleteAttribute('uv'); geo = mergeVertices(geo); // 92 unique verts, connectivity=1.0 — then displace, then set UVs.

Vertex colors for organic assets: compute per-vertex color from the vertex's 3D position using a hash-based noise function — never from buffer index or UV. Position-based noise is seam-free and survives mergeVertices(). Pattern: const colors = new Float32Array(pos.count * 3); for each vertex i, hash its XYZ position to get a noise value, map to palette RGB, write to colors[i*3..i*3+2]. Then: geo.setAttribute('color', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(colors, 3)); material.vertexColors = true. For earthy tones, use a palette of 2–4 colours (e.g. dark-brown shadow, mid-grey, sandy highlight) and lerp between them based on the noise value.

Texture UV seam on image textures: spherical UV projection creates a discontinuity at u=0/u=1 (back of sphere) where adjacent triangle vertices have u≈0 and u≈1. The GPU interpolates across the full [0,1] range within the face, producing a stretched/mirrored artifact. Avoid UV-sampled image textures on round meshes. Prefer: (a) vertex colors computed from 3D position, or (b) a ShaderMaterial / onBeforeCompile that samples texture using world-space position (triplanar) rather than UV. If UV textures are needed, duplicate seam vertices and set u=0 and u=1 explicitly on each copy.

Vertex colors + material base color multiply together. When using vertexColors=true, always set color: 0xffffff on the material so vertex colors are the actual surface color, not a double-darkened tint. Using color: 0x777777 (grey) with vertex colors halves the effective brightness in every channel — under the headless renderer's 0.20 ambient, this pushes shadow pixels below the 20/255 dark-patch threshold, causing false inverted-normal penalties. Pattern: const mat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0xffffff, vertexColors: true, roughness: ..., metalness: ... });

Per-face flat vertex colors (low-poly style): after mergeVertices() and vertex displacement, call geo = geo.toNonIndexed() then geo.computeVertexNormals(). In a non-indexed geometry each vertex belongs to exactly one face, so computeVertexNormals() gives true flat (per-face) normals. Then compute color from the FACE CENTROID (average of the 3 vertex positions) and assign the same RGB to all 3 vertices of each face. This eliminates cross-face color interpolation and gives discrete, faceted color blocks. Pattern: for each face f, cx=(x0+x1+x2)/3, cy=(y0+y1+y2)/3, cz=(z0+z1+z2)/3; compute t=hash(cx,cy,cz); set colors[i0*3], colors[i1*3], colors[i2*3] all to the same (r,g,b). Connectivity scoring uses position keys so toNonIndexed() does NOT reduce shared_edge_fraction.

TubeGeometry with closed=false has OPEN ENDS — boundary edges at both tube ends cause shared_edge_fraction < 0.97 → FAILED. Fix: build a capped tube using custom BufferGeometry with explicit cap triangles. Pattern: (1) use curve.computeFrenetFrames(tubeSeg, false) to get per-ring normals/binormals, (2) push (tubeSeg+1)×radSeg ring vertices into a flat array, (3) push ONE cap-center vertex at curve.getPoint(0) and ONE at curve.getPoint(1), (4) add side quads as two triangles with CORRECT winding idxs.push(a,d,c, a,b,d) — NOT idxs.push(a,c,d, a,d,b) — where a=ring_i[j], b=ring_i[j+1], c=ring_{i+1}[j], d=ring_{i+1}[j+1]; the wrong winding makes both cap-fan and side-quad emit the SAME directed edge at each end ring, so the connectivity check never finds the reverse → sharedFraction drops to 0.926, (5) add start cap fan: idxs.push(startCapIdx,(j+1)%radSeg,j) and end cap fan: idxs.push(endCapIdx,lr+j,lr+(j+1)%radSeg). Then call new THREE.BufferGeometry(), setAttribute position, setIndex, and pass directly to applyFaceColors (which calls toNonIndexed+computeVertexNormals). Do NOT call deleteAttribute or mergeVertices on custom geometry — it is already unique per vertex.

Palette index out-of-bounds crash: Math.floor(noise * palette.length) returns palette.length when noise==1.0 — palette[length] is undefined → reading .r throws. Always clamp: palette[Math.min(Math.floor(noise * palette.length), palette.length - 1)]

Multi-mesh assets must name each significant mesh part using a semantic .name string before adding it to the group. Use standard names so the viewer can apply per-part Realistic materials: 'trunk' or 'bark' for tree trunks/stems/branches, 'foliage' for leaf clusters/canopy, 'body' for the main hull of an object, 'roof', 'ground', 'water', etc. Example: const trunk = new THREE.Mesh(geo, mat); trunk.name = 'trunk'; group.add(trunk);
